title: Snap Unveils $2,195 AR Glasses as Spiegel Pushes Beyond Smartphones
image: /images/news/Snap Unveils $2,195 AR Glasses as Spiegel Pushes Beyond Smartphones.webp

author.name: Alex Thorne
author.bio: Alex covers emerging consumer technologies, augmented reality, and Silicon Valley hardware trends.

excerpt: Snap has introduced its new Specs augmented reality glasses priced at $2,195, as CEO Evan Spiegel doubles down on the belief that AR glasses will eventually replace smartphones as the primary computing platform.

content.text: Snap has officially launched its latest augmented reality device, Specs, marking the company’s most ambitious push yet into wearable computing. The glasses will be priced at $2,195 and are scheduled to begin shipping later this year. The announcement was made during Snap’s annual developer event, where the company showcased a range of new AR experiences and software capabilities.

Chief Executive Evan Spiegel described the launch as a major step toward what he believes will become the next era of personal computing. According to Spiegel, traditional smartphones will eventually be replaced by devices that blend digital information directly into a user's field of vision.

The unveiling positions Snap more aggressively in the growing competition among technology companies developing augmented reality hardware. Major firms across the industry are investing heavily in wearable devices that could become alternatives to smartphones.
The company believes advances in displays, artificial intelligence and spatial computing are creating the conditions necessary for broader adoption of AR technology.
A central theme of Snap’s presentation was the idea that glasses will eventually become the primary way people interact with digital content.

Spiegel argued that wearable devices offer a more natural computing experience because users can access information without constantly looking down at a phone screen. He suggested that augmented reality has the potential to transform communication, entertainment, education and workplace productivity.

The CEO has long promoted the vision of AR becoming a mainstream computing platform, and the latest Specs device represents one of the clearest expressions of that strategy. Snap executives said the company is making investments with a long-term vision, not just focusing on short-term sales volumes, with the goal of developing a hardware and software ecosystem that can support future generations of wearable technology.
The announcement is a sign of growing confidence in the industry that AR devices could eventually occupy a similar position to smartphones today.
New Features Highlight Spatial Computing and AI
The new Specs glasses showcase upgraded displays, enhanced field-of-view technology and boosts in processing power for immersive augmented reality experiences.
Users can interact with digital objects superimposed on the physical world for uses ranging from navigation and gaming to collaboration and content creation.

Snap also demonstrated new artificial intelligence integrations that will offer more natural ways for users to get information and accomplish tasks. AI-powered features are expected to play a big role in future AR experiences by helping devices understand environments and respond to user prompts. The company showed off software that enables developers to build apps that can combine virtual and physical spaces in real time.
Snap believes these capabilities will help expand the range of practical uses for augmented reality while encouraging greater developer participation in its platform.
Competition Intensifies in the AR Hardware Market
The launch comes as competition in the augmented reality sector continues to accelerate.

Technology companies including Apple, Meta and Google are investing billions of dollars in hardware and software aimed at defining the next generation of computing devices. Each company has adopted a different strategy, but all share the belief that wearable technology could eventually become a major platform.

Snap faces big challenges in convincing consumers to buy expensive AR hardware, especially when smartphones are still deeply entrenched in everyday life. The $2,195 price puts Specs squarely in the premium category and wide adoption is unlikely in the near term, analysts say. But supporters say early versions of transformational technologies often launch as high-end products before becoming more affordable.

The Specs launch is about more than selling hardware for Snap. It is a long-term bet that augmented-reality glasses will be the next big computing platform and will eventually change the way people interact with digital technology.
